doc.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022

title: Wlodek Pawlik, Michael's illness and the Grammy-winning record
summary: Pawlik tried to help find a bone-marrow match for Michael; their dedicated record won a Grammy and Brecker re-recorded trumpet at home.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well said. I was pleased to read about this project in Poland that came about because of this fellow who was trying to help Michael out. Can you just tell me a little about that?

Well his name is Wlodek Pawlik and he’s the head of an exceptional musical family. His brother — I mean his son is a wonderful musician. His wife is also a pianist and composer as is Wlodek. And because they’re of Eastern European and Polish descent and our family is also from that area, Mike and people working with him put out feelers to try to get a match for his cancer. It was an area called Tykocin. And our family name on my mother’s side is similar, Tykoski, and the rabbi, the local rabbi’s last name was Tykoski. So when Wlodek caught wind of this I knew him, I had played several tours with some musicians from a college in the Midwest, I forget the name, Wlodek was the piano player and the wife of the bass player was Polish so that’s what the connection was. And the upshot is that Wlodek didn’t find a match, Mike never found a match, which is one of the

reasons he went into such decline as his daughter was a half match. They’re called alleles and the need a match of I think 12 matches. They tried what was called a Haplo identical transplant but it didn’t work. You have to find someone with a match. So Susan, Mike’s wife — getting off the subject here — has spent many years trying to get people to register and register their blood just for this because it’s still a shortage, particularly minorities. And I don’t understand all the science behind it but that’s what I remember at the time. And Wlodek and I had been and became very close friends after I’ve done several projects with him. He’s just a wonderful player and writer, a full time composer. Does a lot of films, probably the foremost film composer in Poland. And we did a record and it won a Grammy that year, kind of dedicated to Mike, and went into the story of the whole story about him trying to find a match and lo and behold it won a Grammy. It was a sweet — the name is escaping me right now.
Tykocin. Yeah. But actually there was one after that. There’s one after that. That’s the one that won the Grammy and gosh it’s terrible I can’t remember the name.
No keep going, it’s right around that time.
Oh it’ll come to me later.

But they all featured Wlodek’s writing and the one I’m thinking about we went over and performed it but he didn’t like the sound and so we re-recorded — we were talking about this stuff earlier. He re-recorded the orchestra and I had to do all the trumpet parts down here in my pajamas and make it fit over the orchestra. But you know it won a Grammy so I was wearing the right kind of pajamas.
